suggested_new_group.reason_existing_groups_insufficient: Existing combat groups emphasize divine warriors, sacred warfare, or threshold guardians; they do not clearly hold non-divine heroic monster-slaying episodes where the creature is the central ordeal.

label: Monstrous harbour obstruction overcome by heroes
rationale: A monster obstructing a harbor functions as a liminal passage-blocker that heroes must overcome to proceed.
cautions: If the main emphasis is heroic monster-slaying rather than blocked passage, a monster_combat candidate may be preferable.

label: monstrous hunger causing food theft or pollution
rationale: Monstrous appetite and food pollution may function as disorder, taboo violation, or social contamination, but the label is too composite for a clear group.
cautions: Could map to chaos, sacred_law, trickster, or divine_judgment if evidence clarifies whether pollution, transgression, or punishment is central.

label: monstrous husband or pursuer demands battle
rationale: The central action is a demanded combat challenge by a threatening pursuer or spouse, fitting sacred/heroic combat patterns.
cautions: If the marital pursuit or abduction is the core motif, a family/love conflict group may be needed; current label may be episode-specific.

label: monstrous many-limbed primordial giants
rationale: Primordial giants belong to the pre-cosmic or early-cosmic field of chaos and origin, with monstrous form marking disorder before stable order.
cautions: If the passage emphasizes battle against them, secondary placement under divine_warrior or sacred_combat may be appropriate.

label: monstrous one-eyed guardian with conditional death
rationale: A monstrous guardian with a special death condition functions as a boundary obstacle to be confronted or overcome.
cautions: The conditional-death element may also overlap with external_soul if life is bound to an external condition or token; review source details.

label: monstrous or animal-headed enemy peoples
rationale: Animal-headed peoples may reflect hybrid transformation, monstrous enemy imagery, or ethnographic othering rather than shapeshifting.
cautions: Single occurrence and culturally sensitive enemy/monstrous labeling; verify whether these are beings with transformed bodies, demonized peoples, or passage-specific rhetoric.

label: Monstrous recurrence of civic evils
rationale: Recurring civic evils suggest moral disorder requiring reckoning or repair within a sacred-social order.
cautions: The word monstrous may be metaphorical; if this is only civic commentary rather than mythic action, human review may exclude or remap to sacred_law.

label: monstrous sea hazard at a dangerous strait
rationale: A monster or hazard at a strait functions as a perilous threshold blocking passage.
cautions: If the emphasis is heroic combat rather than guarded passage, sacred_combat or divine_warrior may be secondary; preserve sea-strait detail as evidence.

label: Monstrous sisters at the edge of the world
rationale: Monstrous figures at the world edge mark a liminal boundary that must be approached, avoided, or overcome.
cautions: Could also relate to otherworld, sacred combat, or sibling-pair imagery depending on whether the sisters guard a passage, threaten a hero, or simply inhabit a far region.

label: monumental cult image of the solar god
rationale: The label may describe a cult object, solar theophany, divine image, or place-specific monument, and the motif function is unclear.
cautions: Could be too specific or object/place-focused for pattern queries; map to sacred_treasures only if the image has active sacred power, or to theophany/sacred_fire if solar manifestation is central.
suggested_aliases: cult statue of the sun god

label: monumental grave for a fallen hero
rationale: A monumental grave for a fallen hero is a memorial act honoring heroic death and reaffirming social memory.
cautions: If the grave becomes a sacred center or cult site, secondary mapping to world_center or ancestor_rites may be useful.

label: Moon as guide and comforter
rationale: The moon functions as a celestial presence offering guidance and emotional support, not covered well by existing water, vision, or divine-intervention groups.
cautions: May be poetic personification rather than a durable motif; review alongside other sun, moon, star guide or witness labels before adding a group.

suggested_new_group.label: Celestial Guides and Witnesses
suggested_new_group.description: Celestial bodies such as moon, sun, stars, or planets act as guides, witnesses, comforters, omens, or companions in human or sacred journeys.
suggested_new_group.reason_existing_groups_insufficient: Existing groups include cosmic vision and cosmic witness, but no broad group for recurring celestial bodies acting as guides, witnesses, or affective companions outside formal vision or duality motifs.

label: Moon as witness to future absence
rationale: The moon serves as a witness to longing and absence, a celestial-personified witness motif.
cautions: Could belong under sacred_love if the passage centers on beloved absence; do not promote a celestial group unless similar sun/moon/star witness labels recur.

suggested_new_group.label: Celestial Guides and Witnesses
suggested_new_group.description: Celestial bodies such as moon, sun, stars, or planets act as guides, witnesses, comforters, omens, or companions in human or sacred journeys.
suggested_new_group.reason_existing_groups_insufficient: Existing groups include cosmic witness under duality and dream/vision signs, but they do not cleanly hold poetic or devotional celestial witnessing of absence and longing.

label: Moon-marked abducted water-carrying children
rationale: The label combines abduction, lunar marking, children, and water-carrying without enough evidence to identify the dominant motif function.

label: Moral causality as sowing and harvest
rationale: The label uses agricultural imagery to express moral consequence or reckoning, which fits divine or sacred moral causality.
cautions: If the passage is primarily ethical teaching rather than judgment, sacred_knowledge or sacred_law may be a secondary fit.

label: Moral community enjoining good and forbidding wrong
rationale: The motif centers on communal ethical obligation grounded in sacred law and moral order.
cautions: May also support covenant or wisdom if the passage emphasizes divine command or instruction rather than communal practice.

label: Moral corruption spreading from leaders to people
rationale: The label concerns the moral condition of rulers affecting the social body, a sacred kingship and legitimate-rule concern.

label: Moral decline of an age or race

label: Moral decline through loss of a guardian

label: moral reciprocity of good and ill
rationale: Good and ill returning reciprocally is an ethical-order motif, close to sacred law and moral consequence.

label: moral reform through corrective instruction
rationale: Corrective instruction producing moral reform fits wisdom teaching as transformative knowledge.

label: Moralized conflict of virtue and vice

label: moralized forbidden or rash youthful love

label: Moralized paired waters of falsehood and truth

label: Morning floral abundance

label: mortal challenges deity in craft contest

label: mortal god with grave

label: mortal granted perception of gods

label: mortal transformed into sea-divinity after entering the sea
